AStar2D.get_available_point_id: Returns the next available point ID with no point associated to it.

AStar2D.connect_points: Creates a segment between the given points.
AStar2D.disconnect_points: Deletes the segment between the given points.
AStar2D.are_points_connected: Returns whether there is a connection/segment between the given points.

AStar2D.reserve_space: Reserves space internally for num_nodes points.
AStar2D.clear: Clears all the points and segments.
AStar2D.get_closest_point: Returns the ID of the closest point to to_position, optionally taking disabled points into account.
AStar2D.get_closest_position_in_segment: Returns the closest position to to_position that resides inside a segment between two connected points.
AStar2D.get_point_path: Returns an array with the points that are in the path found by AStar2D between the given points.
AStar2D.get_id_path: Returns an array with the IDs of the points that form the path found by AStar2D between the given points.

AStar2D: An implementation of A* for finding the shortest path between two vertices on a connected graph in 2D space.

ParticleProcessMaterial..spread: Each particle's initial direction range from +spread to -spread degrees.
ParticleProcessMaterial..flatness: Amount of spread along the Y axis.
ParticleProcessMaterial..initial_velocity_max: Maximum initial velocity magnitude for each particle.
ParticleProcessMaterial..angular_velocity_max: Maximum initial angular velocity (rotation speed) applied to each particle in degrees per second.
ParticleProcessMaterial..angular_velocity_curve: Each particle's angular velocity (rotation speed) will vary along this CurveTexture over its lifetime.
ParticleProcessMaterial..directional_velocity_min: Minimum directional velocity value, which is multiplied by directional_velocity_curve.
ParticleProcessMaterial..directional_velocity_max: Maximum directional velocity value, which is multiplied by directional_velocity_curve.
ParticleProcessMaterial..directional_velocity_curve: A curve that specifies the velocity along each of the axes of the particle system along its lifetime.
ParticleProcessMaterial..orbit_velocity_max: Maximum orbital velocity applied to each particle.
ParticleProcessMaterial..orbit_velocity_curve: Each particle's orbital velocity will vary along this CurveTexture.
ParticleProcessMaterial..radial_velocity_min: Minimum radial velocity applied to each particle.
ParticleProcessMaterial..radial_velocity_max: Maximum radial velocity applied to each particle.
ParticleProcessMaterial..radial_velocity_curve: A CurveTexture that defines the velocity over the particle's lifetime away (or toward) the velocity_pivot.
ParticleProcessMaterial..velocity_limit_curve: A CurveTexture that defines the maximum velocity of a particle during its lifetime.
ParticleProcessMaterial..rotation_velocity_3d_min: Minimum 3D rotation velocity on the particle's local axis.
ParticleProcessMaterial..rotation_velocity_3d_max: Maximum 3D rotation velocity on the particle's local axis.
ParticleProcessMaterial..rotation_velocity_3d_curve: Rotation velocity curve over lifetime, per-axis.
ParticleProcessMaterial..linear_accel_max: Maximum linear acceleration applied to each particle in the direction of motion.
ParticleProcessMaterial..linear_accel_curve: Each particle's linear acceleration will vary along this CurveTexture.
ParticleProcessMaterial..radial_accel_max: Maximum radial acceleration applied to each particle.
ParticleProcessMaterial..radial_accel_curve: Each particle's radial acceleration will vary along this CurveTexture.
ParticleProcessMaterial..tangential_accel_max: Maximum tangential acceleration applied to each particle.
ParticleProcessMaterial..tangential_accel_curve: Each particle's tangential acceleration will vary along this CurveTexture.
ParticleProcessMaterial..damping_max: The maximum rate at which particles lose velocity.
ParticleProcessMaterial..damping_curve: Damping will vary along this CurveTexture.
ParticleProcessMaterial..attractor_interaction_enabled: If true, interaction with particle attractors is enabled.
ParticleProcessMaterial..use_scale_3d: Enable the usage of scale_3d_min and scale_3d_max.
ParticleProcessMaterial..scale_3d_min: The minimum value of the random scale vector for each particle.
ParticleProcessMaterial..scale_3d_max: The maximum value of the random scale vector for each particle.
ParticleProcessMaterial..scale_max: Maximum initial scale applied to each particle.
ParticleProcessMaterial..scale_curve: Each particle's scale will vary along this CurveTexture over its lifetime.
ParticleProcessMaterial..scale_over_velocity_min: Minimum velocity value reference for scale_over_velocity_curve.
ParticleProcessMaterial..scale_over_velocity_max: Maximum velocity value reference for scale_over_velocity_curve.
ParticleProcessMaterial..scale_over_velocity_curve: Either a CurveTexture or a CurveXYZTexture that scales each particle based on its velocity.
ParticleProcessMaterial..color_ramp: Each particle's color will vary along this GradientTexture1D over its lifetime (multiplied with color).
ParticleProcessMaterial..color_initial_ramp: Each particle's initial color will vary along this GradientTexture1D (multiplied with color).
ParticleProcessMaterial..alpha_curve: The alpha value of each particle's color will be multiplied by this CurveTexture over its lifetime.
ParticleProcessMaterial..emission_curve: Each particle's color will be multiplied by this CurveTexture over its lifetime.
ParticleProcessMaterial..hue_variation_max: Maximum initial hue variation applied to each particle.
ParticleProcessMaterial..hue_variation_curve: Each particle's hue will vary along this CurveTexture.
ParticleProcessMaterial..anim_speed_curve: Each particle's animation speed will vary along this CurveTexture.
ParticleProcessMaterial..anim_offset_max: Maximum animation offset that corresponds to frame index in the texture.
ParticleProcessMaterial..anim_offset_curve: Each particle's animation offset will vary along this CurveTexture.
ParticleProcessMaterial..turbulence_enabled: If true, enables turbulence for the particle system.
ParticleProcessMaterial..turbulence_noise_scale: This value controls the overall scale/frequency of the turbulence noise pattern.
ParticleProcessMaterial..turbulence_noise_speed: A scrolling velocity for the turbulence field.
ParticleProcessMaterial..turbulence_noise_speed_random: The in-place rate of change of the turbulence field.
ParticleProcessMaterial..turbulence_influence_min: Minimum turbulence influence on each particle.
ParticleProcessMaterial..turbulence_influence_max: Maximum turbulence influence on each particle.
ParticleProcessMaterial..turbulence_initial_displacement_min: Minimum displacement of each particle's spawn position by the turbulence.
ParticleProcessMaterial..turbulence_initial_displacement_max: Maximum displacement of each particle's spawn position by the turbulence.
ParticleProcessMaterial..turbulence_influence_over_life: Each particle's amount of turbulence will be influenced along this CurveTexture over its life time.
ParticleProcessMaterial..collision_use_scale: If true, GPUParticles3D.collision_base_size is multiplied by the particle's effective scale (see scale_min, scale_max, scale_curve, and scale_over_velocity_curve).
ParticleProcessMaterial..sub_emitter_mode: The particle subemitter mode (see GPUParticles2D.sub_emitter and GPUParticles3D.sub_emitter).
ParticleProcessMaterial..sub_emitter_frequency: The frequency at which particles should be emitted from the subemitter node.
ParticleProcessMaterial..sub_emitter_amount_at_end: The amount of particles to spawn from the subemitter node when the particle expires.
ParticleProcessMaterial..sub_emitter_amount_at_collision: The amount of particles to spawn from the subemitter node when a collision occurs.
ParticleProcessMaterial..sub_emitter_amount_at_start: The amount of particles to spawn from the subemitter node when the particle spawns.
ParticleProcessMaterial..sub_emitter_keep_velocity: If true, the subemitter inherits the parent particle's velocity when it spawns.
ParticleProcessMaterial.!emission_shape_changed: Emitted when this material's emission shape is changed in any way.
ParticleProcessMaterial: Holds a particle configuration for GPUParticles2D or GPUParticles3D nodes.

Path2D: Contains a Curve2D path for PathFollow2D nodes to follow.

Path3D..debug_custom_color: The custom color used to draw the path in the editor.
Path3D: Contains a Curve3D path for PathFollow3D nodes to follow.

PathFollow2D..progress: The distance along the path, in pixels.
PathFollow2D..progress_ratio: The distance along the path as a number in the range 0.0 (for the first vertex) to 1.0 (for the last).
PathFollow2D..h_offset: The node's offset along the curve.
PathFollow2D..v_offset: The node's offset perpendicular to the curve.
PathFollow2D..rotates: If true, this node rotates to follow the path, with the +X direction facing forward on the path.
PathFollow2D..cubic_interp: If true, the position between two cached points is interpolated cubically, and linearly otherwise.
PathFollow2D..loop: If true, any offset outside the path's length will wrap around, instead of stopping at the ends.

PathFollow3D..progress: The distance from the first vertex, measured in 3D units along the path.
PathFollow3D..progress_ratio: The distance from the first vertex, considering 0.0 as the first vertex and 1.0 as the last.
PathFollow3D..h_offset: The node's offset along the curve.
PathFollow3D..v_offset: The node's offset perpendicular to the curve.
PathFollow3D..rotation_mode: Allows or forbids rotation on one or more axes, depending on the RotationMode constants being used.
PathFollow3D..use_model_front: If true, the node moves on the travel path with orienting the +Z axis as forward.
PathFollow3D..cubic_interp: If true, the position between two cached points is interpolated cubically, and linearly otherwise.
PathFollow3D..loop: If true, any offset outside the path's length will wrap around, instead of stopping at the ends.
PathFollow3D..tilt_enabled: If true, the tilt property of Curve3D takes effect.

Performance.get_monitor: Returns the value of one of the available built-in monitors.
Performance.add_custom_monitor: Adds a custom monitor with the name id.
Performance.remove_custom_monitor: Removes the custom monitor with given id.
Performance.has_custom_monitor: Returns true if custom monitor with the given id is present, false otherwise.
Performance.get_custom_monitor: Returns the value of custom monitor with given id.
Performance.get_monitor_modification_time: Returns the last tick in which custom monitor was added/removed (in microseconds since the engine started).
Performance.get_custom_monitor_names: Returns the names of active custom monitors in an Array.
Performance.get_custom_monitor_types: Returns the MonitorType values of active custom monitors in an Array.

PhysXBlastAsset.get_chunk_count: Returns how many chunks this asset has, including chunk 0 (the whole unfractured mesh) -- so this is always one more than the number of pieces a full fracture actually produces.
PhysXBlastAsset..asset_bytes: The raw NvBlast asset data (bond/chunk support-graph structure) -- a single relocatable memory block per NvBlast's own design, stored here as-is.
PhysXBlastAsset..chunk_points: Per-chunk render-mesh triangle-soup positions, in the source mesh's local space -- one PackedVector3Array per chunk, index-matched to asset_bytes' own chunk indices.
PhysXBlastAsset: A fractured mesh, ready to drive a PhysXDestructible3D.

PhysXBlastAuthoring.fracture_mesh: Fractures surface 0 of mesh and returns the result, or null on failure.
PhysXBlastAuthoring: Fractures meshes into Blast assets for PhysXDestructible3D.

PhysXBoat3D.get_forward_speed: Speed along the keel (m/s); negative going astern.
PhysXBoat3D.get_applied_thrust: The propeller's thrust this physics tick (N, negative astern); 0 while the propeller is out of the water.
PhysXBoat3D..steering: -1..1: positive turns left (as VehicleBody3D.steering), turning the propeller up to max_steer_angle.
PhysXBoat3D..max_thrust: Propeller thrust (N) at full throttle ahead.
PhysXBoat3D..reverse_thrust_ratio: Thrust astern as a fraction of max_thrust.
PhysXBoat3D..max_steer_angle: How far the propeller turns at full steering.
PhysXBoat3D..propeller_position: Where the propeller is, in the body's space: at the stern, below the waterline.
PhysXBoat3D..rudder_strength: Side force from water flowing across the propeller's leg (N per (m/s)²).
PhysXBoat3D..propeller_wash_speed: Speed (m/s) of the propeller's wash over its leg at full throttle -- what lets the boat steer under power even at a standstill.
PhysXBoat3D..hull_drag: Quadratic hull drag (N per (m/s)²) in the boat's frame: x sideways, y vertical, z along the keel.
PhysXBoat3D..hull_linear_drag: Linear hull drag (N per m/s), same axes as hull_drag -- settles slow drifting, where quadratic drag fades away.
PhysXBoat3D..angular_damping: Rotational damping (N·m per rad/s) in the boat's frame: x pitch, y yaw, z roll.
PhysXBoat3D: Drives its parent RigidBody3D as a powered boat.

PhysXBuoyancy3D.get_submerged_fraction: How much of the hull's buoyancy is in use this physics tick: 0 out of the water, 1 fully under.
PhysXBuoyancy3D.get_point_depths: Each sample point's depth below the water surface this physics tick (m); 0 or less is above it, -INF where there is no water.
PhysXBuoyancy3D.get_effective_sample_points: The sample points in use, in the body's space: sample_points, or the generated ones.
PhysXBuoyancy3D.get_water_height: The water surface height at world_pos (see PhysXWaterSurface3D.sample_height); -INF where there is no water.
PhysXBuoyancy3D..sample_points: Points on the hull, in the body's space, where the water pushes.
PhysXBuoyancy3D..hull_area: The hull's footprint on the water (m²), shared between the sample points.
PhysXBuoyancy3D..hull_height: How deep (m) the hull can sink before the push stops growing -- the depth at which it is fully under.
PhysXBuoyancy3D..linear_drag: Drag on each submerged point against its velocity (N per m/s per m² of footprint, scaled by how deep it is).
PhysXBuoyancy3D..angular_drag: Damping on the body's rotation (N·m per rad/s), scaled by how much of the hull is in the water.
PhysXBuoyancy3D..disturb_water: Push the water's ripple layer where the body floats, more as it moves.
PhysXBuoyancy3D..ripple_radius: Radius (m) of the body's disturbance in the ripple layer.
PhysXBuoyancy3D..ripple_rest_strength: Disturbance strength when the body is still (0..1) -- a small, steady dimple; it ramps up to full strength at ripple_reference_speed.
PhysXBuoyancy3D..ripple_reference_speed: Speed (m/s) at which the body's disturbance reaches full strength.
PhysXBuoyancy3D: Floats its parent RigidBody3D on a PhysXWaterSurface3D.

PhysXChunkEmitter3D.spawn_at: Bursts count chunks (or chunk_count when count is negative) from world_position, scattered within a spread_degrees cone around direction -- pass a surface normal for an impact, or use a wide spread_degrees for a non-dire
PhysXChunkEmitter3D.get_active_chunk_count: Returns the number of chunks currently alive.
PhysXChunkEmitter3D..chunk_count: Chunks spawned per spawn_at call, unless overridden by its count argument.
PhysXChunkEmitter3D..chunk_size_min: Lower bound of a chunk's random size, in meters.
PhysXChunkEmitter3D..chunk_size_max: Upper bound of a chunk's random size, in meters (edge length for SHAPE_BOX, diameter for SHAPE_SPHERE).
PhysXChunkEmitter3D..chunk_shape: Collision shape (and default chunk_mesh) used for every chunk.
PhysXChunkEmitter3D..chunk_mesh: Mesh drawn for each chunk, shared by every instance via one MultiMesh.
PhysXChunkEmitter3D..impulse_min: Lower bound of a chunk's initial speed, in m/s.
PhysXChunkEmitter3D..impulse_max: Upper bound of a chunk's initial speed, in m/s.
PhysXChunkEmitter3D..spread_degrees: Half-angle, in degrees, of the cone chunks fly out in around the burst direction.
PhysXChunkEmitter3D..spin_impulse: Upper bound of a chunk's random initial angular velocity, in rad/s.
PhysXChunkEmitter3D..density: Chunk density in kg/m³, used with each chunk's random size to derive its mass.
PhysXChunkEmitter3D..friction: Surface friction of every chunk (matches the space's default material).
PhysXChunkEmitter3D..linear_damp: Linear damping applied to every chunk, on top of friction.
PhysXChunkEmitter3D..angular_damp: Angular damping applied to every chunk.
PhysXChunkEmitter3D..lifetime: Seconds a chunk lives before it is recycled, even if max_active has not been reached.
PhysXChunkEmitter3D..shrink_time: Seconds before a chunk's natural lifetime end during which it scales down to nothing instead of popping.
PhysXChunkEmitter3D..max_active: Hard cap on chunks alive at once, across every burst and continuous emission from this emitter.
PhysXChunkEmitter3D..emitting: When true, continuously spawns chunks from the node's own position at emission_rate, instead of (or alongside) calling spawn_at for one-off bursts.
PhysXChunkEmitter3D..emission_rate: Chunks spawned per second while emitting.
PhysXChunkEmitter3D..emission_direction: World-space direction chunks are biased toward while emitting, within a spread_degrees cone.
PhysXChunkEmitter3D..collision_mask: Physics layers the chunks collide with.
PhysXChunkEmitter3D: A general-purpose burst of small rigid-body chunks, provided by the PhysX module.

PhysXCloth3D.reset: Drops the cloth back to its rest shape at the node's current transform.
PhysXCloth3D.get_vertex_count: Returns the number of simulated vertices.
PhysXCloth3D.get_pinned_positions: Returns the current positions of the pinned vertices, in this node's local space, in the order they were pinned.
PhysXCloth3D.is_gpu_accelerated: Returns true when the GPU deformable-surface path is in use rather than the CPU XPBD fallback.
PhysXCloth3D..source_mesh: A triangle mesh to simulate instead of a generated grid.
PhysXCloth3D..grid_size: Size of the generated grid in meters, centered on the node in its local XY plane (facing +Z).
PhysXCloth3D..simulating: When false the cloth freezes in place.
PhysXCloth3D..stiffness: Resistance to stretching along the weave, from 0 (elastic) to 1 (inextensible).
PhysXCloth3D..shear_stiffness: Resistance to in-plane skewing, from 0 to 1.
PhysXCloth3D..damping: Fraction of velocity removed per second.
PhysXCloth3D..density: Areal mass in kg/m², used to weight the vertices.
PhysXCloth3D..wind_enabled: Master switch for all air forces (wind, wind_area, drag, lift).
PhysXCloth3D..wind_area: An Area3D whose wind settings (force, source, attenuation) drive the cloth.
PhysXCloth3D..wind: A constant world-space air velocity, added on top of any wind_area.
PhysXCloth3D..wind_turbulence: Adds a swirling gust on top of the steady wind, as a fraction of its speed.
PhysXCloth3D..drag: How hard air pushes on a triangle face-on.
PhysXCloth3D..lift: Sideways push from air flowing across a triangle, which makes slack cloth ripple.
PhysXCloth3D..pin_mode: A quick way to fix an edge or the corners of a generated grid in place.
PhysXCloth3D..pinned_vertices: Extra vertices to fix in place, by index, on top of pin_mode.
PhysXCloth3D..anchor_path: Optional Node3D the pinned vertices follow: as it moves and rotates, so do the pins, so the cloth can hang off an animated object.
PhysXCloth3D..collision_enabled: When enabled, each vertex is pushed out of any physics body it overlaps each step.
PhysXCloth3D..collision_mask: Physics layers the cloth collides with.
PhysXCloth3D..collision_friction: Fraction of a vertex's sideways velocity removed while it is touching a surface, from 0 (frictionless) to 1.
PhysXCloth3D: A simulated cloth patch, provided by the PhysX module.

PhysXDestructible3D.apply_radial_damage: Applies damage to every bond within max_radius of world_position, at full strength inside min_radius and falling off linearly to zero at max_radius.
PhysXDestructible3D..asset_path: Legacy loading path: a .asset file (raw NvBlastAsset bytes), paired with chunks_path.
PhysXDestructible3D..chunks_path: Legacy loading path: a .chunks text file (per-chunk render-mesh triangle soup), paired with asset_path.
PhysXDestructible3D..blast_asset: The fractured mesh data to use, saved by the in-editor fracture dialog (or PhysXBlastAuthoring directly).
PhysXDestructible3D..material_override: Material applied to every piece's render mesh, intact or fractured, in place of the source mesh's own materials (which aren't carried over by the fracture process).
PhysXDestructible3D..material_overlay: A second material layered on top of every piece's render mesh, the same as GeometryInstance3D.material_overlay -- decals, damage overlays, and the like, without replacing the base material the way material_override does.
PhysXDestructible3D..transparency: Transparency of the rendered chunks, from 0.0 (opaque) to 1.0 (invisible), like GeometryInstance3D.transparency.
PhysXDestructible3D..cast_shadow: Shadow-casting behavior for every piece's render mesh, the same four settings as GeometryInstance3D.cast_shadow.
PhysXDestructible3D..gi_mode: Controls VoxelGI baking for every piece's render mesh, the same two settings as GeometryInstance3D.gi_mode.
PhysXDestructible3D..extra_cull_margin: Widens the bounds used for frustum culling on every piece, the same as GeometryInstance3D.extra_cull_margin.
PhysXDestructible3D..lod_bias: Mesh LOD selection bias for every piece, the same as GeometryInstance3D.lod_bias.
PhysXDestructible3D..ignore_occlusion_culling: When true, every piece is exempt from occlusion culling, the same as GeometryInstance3D.ignore_occlusion_culling.
PhysXDestructible3D..visibility_range_begin: Distance from the camera at which every piece starts being visible, the same as GeometryInstance3D.visibility_range_begin.
PhysXDestructible3D..visibility_range_begin_margin: Fade transition distance for visibility_range_begin, the same as GeometryInstance3D.visibility_range_begin_margin.
PhysXDestructible3D..visibility_range_end: Distance from the camera beyond which every piece stops being visible, the same as GeometryInstance3D.visibility_range_end.
PhysXDestructible3D..visibility_range_end_margin: Fade transition distance for visibility_range_end, the same as GeometryInstance3D.visibility_range_end_margin.
PhysXDestructible3D..visibility_range_fade_mode: How pieces fade in/out at the edges of visibility_range_begin/visibility_range_end, the same as GeometryInstance3D.visibility_range_fade_mode.
PhysXDestructible3D..shatter_speed: Speed (m/s, before falloff) each newly detached piece is kicked away from the damage origin -- see apply_radial_damage's own note on the exact direction/falloff shape.
PhysXDestructible3D..collision_layer: Physics layers this object (intact or fractured) occupies, same meaning as CollisionObject3D.collision_layer.
PhysXDestructible3D..collision_mask: Physics layers this object (intact or fractured) collides with, same meaning as CollisionObject3D.collision_mask.
PhysXDestructible3D..auto_mass: When true, mass is recomputed from the intact mesh's real volume (times its node scale) every time the asset (re)loads, and shown read-only in the Inspector -- "here's what this object would actually weigh." Uncheck it f
PhysXDestructible3D..mass: The whole intact object's mass, same meaning as RigidBody3D.mass.
PhysXDestructible3D..dynamic: When true, the intact object is a real falling/colliding rigid body instead of a fixed prop, and a hard enough physical collision auto-fractures it (see impact_strength / impact_damage_scale / impact_radius).
PhysXDestructible3D..health: How much cumulative damage each bond in the fracture structure can absorb before it breaks -- see the class description's "How damage, health, and radius actually interact" section for the full picture.
PhysXDestructible3D..impact_strength: dynamic-only. The minimum contact impulse (roughly mass × velocity change, in Godot's physics units) that counts as an impact worth reacting to at all -- landing softly or a gentle bump below this is ignored entirely, no
PhysXDestructible3D..impact_damage_scale: dynamic-only. Once a collision's impulse clears impact_strength, this scales how much extra damage the excess produces: damage = (impulse - impact_strength) * impact_damage_scale (before the health × 1.5 floor -- see app
PhysXDestructible3D..impact_radius: dynamic-only. The max_radius passed to the auto-triggered apply_radial_damage call on a qualifying impact, centered on the contact point (min_radius is always 0 for this path -- full damage right at the contact, falling
PhysXDestructible3D..kill_y: A piece (fractured debris, or the intact body itself if dynamic) whose world-space Y position falls below this is freed automatically.
PhysXDestructible3D: A mesh that fractures into real rigid-body debris at runtime, provided by the PhysX module's NvBlast integration.

PhysXFlow3D.sample_smoke: The smoke at position (world space), from the last CPU readback.
PhysXFlow3D.is_running: Whether Flow is running for this node (see the configuration warnings if not).
PhysXFlow3D.get_stats: Diagnostics: running, error, start_ms (grid creation), step_ms, render_calls, render_outputs, readback_bytes, bounds (the gas, with cpu_readback), active_blocks (sparse blocks in use, of max_blocks), and Flow's pipeline
PhysXFlow3D..max_blocks: The most sparse blocks the gas may take up -- a GPU memory budget, since Flow reserves memory for all of them when the grid starts (about 0.45 MB a block: the default 1024 is roughly 0.5 GB).
PhysXFlow3D..buoyancy: Upward acceleration per unit of temperature: hot gas rises, cool gas hangs.
PhysXFlow3D..cooling_rate: How fast the gas cools (exponential, per second).
PhysXFlow3D..smoke_fade: How fast smoke thins out (per second).
PhysXFlow3D..vorticity: Vorticity confinement: keeps small swirls alive for rolling, billowing gas.
PhysXFlow3D..combustion: Fuel burns when hotter than ignition_temperature, releasing heat and smoke.
PhysXFlow3D..ignition_temperature: The temperature above which fuel burns (see combustion).
PhysXFlow3D..collide_with_bodies: Physics bodies near the gas become solids for it.
PhysXFlow3D..collision_mask: The physics layers whose bodies the gas collides with.
PhysXFlow3D..collision_range: How far from this flow's emitters (in meters) bodies are looked for.
PhysXFlow3D..smoke_density: Opacity per meter, per unit of smoke.
PhysXFlow3D..smoke_color: The smoke's color, lit by the scene's sun: white steam, gray or black smoke, brown dust, colored signal smoke.
PhysXFlow3D..smoke_ramp: The smoke's color by temperature, from 0 to temperature_range -- e.g.
PhysXFlow3D..heat_ramp: How the gas glows by temperature, from 0 to temperature_range: each color is the glow at that temperature, its alpha how much it glows instead of showing the lit smoke.
PhysXFlow3D..temperature_range: The temperature at the end of heat_ramp.
PhysXFlow3D..emission_strength: How bright the heat_ramp glow is.
PhysXFlow3D..shadow_steps: How far the self-shadowing reaches toward the light, in steps of three quarters of a cell (48 is about 1.8 m at the default cell_size).
PhysXFlow3D..cpu_readback: Copy temperature and smoke back to the CPU every few steps, for sample_smoke and the bounds in get_stats.
PhysXFlow3D: NVIDIA Flow smoke, fire and dust, provided by the PhysX module.

PhysXFlowEmitter3D.get_motion_velocity: This node's world-space velocity over the last physics step (what a solid pushes into the gas).
PhysXFlowEmitter3D.get_flow: The PhysXFlow3D this emitter feeds right now, or null.
PhysXFlowEmitter3D..collision: Make this a solid the gas flows around, moving with this node, instead of a source.
PhysXFlowEmitter3D..velocity: Velocity put in, in this node's own frame (a nozzle turns with the node), in m/s.
PhysXFlowEmitter3D..temperature: Temperature put in: hot gas rises and glows (see PhysXFlow3D.heat_ramp).
PhysXFlowEmitter3D..fuel: Fuel put in; it burns above the flow's PhysXFlow3D.ignition_temperature, making heat and smoke.
PhysXFlowEmitter3D..burn: Burn amount put in (combustion that is already under way).
PhysXFlowEmitter3D..divergence: Expansion put in: positive pushes gas outward, as from an explosion.
PhysXFlowEmitter3D..couple_rate: How strongly the emitter drives the gas toward its values (per second).
PhysXFlowEmitter3D: A source of smoke, heat and fuel for a PhysXFlow3D, or a solid in it.

PhysXFlowRenderEffect.get_world_compositor: The Compositor world renders with, which World3D doesn't expose to scripts.
PhysXFlowRenderEffect: Draws every PhysXFlow3D into the frame.

PhysXGas3D.is_domain_configured: Returns true once the solver has fixed its simulation box in world space.
PhysXGas3D.get_configured_domain_anchor: Returns the world position of the minimum corner of the simulation box, once the solver has fixed it (see is_domain_configured).
PhysXGas3D.get_configured_domain_size: Returns the current world-space size of the simulation box.
PhysXGas3D.get_last_max_density: Returns the highest gas density in the last rendered update.
PhysXGas3D..domain_size: World size of the fixed grid box, centered on the node.
PhysXGas3D..emitters: Up to 4 Node3D paths, each an injection point.
PhysXGas3D..emitter_radius: Fallback sphere radius (meters) for entries in emitters that are not a PhysXGasEmitter3D.
PhysXGas3D..emitter_velocity: Fallback world-space injected velocity for entries in emitters that are not a PhysXGasEmitter3D, plus a small per-cell random jitter scaled by its magnitude -- a perfectly symmetric emitter gives vorticity confinement no
PhysXGas3D..emitter_density: Fallback injected density for entries in emitters that are not a PhysXGasEmitter3D (clamped up to at least this, never down -- an emitter tops a cell up, it does not overwrite a denser one).
PhysXGas3D..buoyancy: Upward acceleration applied to a cell's velocity, scaled by its own density.
PhysXGas3D..vorticity_strength: Vorticity confinement strength -- pumps energy back into small eddies the grid's own numerical diffusion would otherwise smear away.
PhysXGas3D..dissipation: Per-step density multiplier (how fast the gas fades).
PhysXGas3D..turbulence_strength: Extra curl-noise perturbation velocity (m/s), added only to the advection sample, not the real solved field.
PhysXGas3D..turbulence_scale: Spatial frequency (1/meters) of turbulence_strength's base octave -- higher values give finer, tighter wrinkles; lower values give broader, slower-rolling ones.
PhysXGas3D..colliders: Up to 4 Node3D paths; each one's global position drives a sphere obstacle.
PhysXGas3D..collider_radius: Fallback radius (meters) for entries in colliders that are not a sphere-shaped CollisionShape3D/CollisionObject3D.
PhysXGas3D..volumetric_render: Draws the gas through a FogVolume + FogMaterial (see the class description for the Environment.volumetric_fog_enabled requirement).
PhysXGas3D..fog_density: FogMaterial.density on the managed FogMaterial -- multiplies the solver's raw density values (roughly 0..1) to a visible opacity.
PhysXGas3D..fog_albedo: FogMaterial.albedo on the managed FogMaterial -- the smoke's scattering colour.
PhysXGas3D..fire_look: Swaps the plain gray FogMaterial for a custom shader that maps the SAME density field through fire_color_ramp with emission, instead of a flat colour -- a cheap way to hint at underlying fire (an explosion/fireball) with
PhysXGas3D..fire_color_ramp: The colour ramp fire_look samples by (normalized) density -- a cell's colour is wherever on this gradient its density falls.
PhysXGas3D..fire_emission_strength: How brightly the hot part of the cloud glows (self-illuminates) when fire_look is on.
PhysXGas3D..debug_point_cloud: Also (or instead) draws a debug point cloud (a MultiMesh of small cubes, one per grid cell above render_threshold, colour-ramped by density) -- useful to sanity-check the raw simulation data against the shaded volumetric
PhysXGas3D..render_threshold: Minimum density for a cell to appear in debug_point_cloud.
PhysXGas3D: A sparse-grid Eulerian smoke/gas volume, provided by the PhysX module.

PhysXGasEmitter3D..enabled: Disables the emitter without removing it from PhysXGas3D.emitters.
PhysXGasEmitter3D..shape: SHAPE_SPHERE (uses radius) or SHAPE_BOX (uses size, axis-aligned -- see the class description).
PhysXGasEmitter3D..radius: Sphere radius in meters, used when shape is SHAPE_SPHERE.
PhysXGasEmitter3D..size: Box full size in meters (halved internally), used when shape is SHAPE_BOX.
PhysXGasEmitter3D..velocity: Injected velocity each step, in this node's local space (rotated, not scaled, by its global orientation -- orient the node to aim the jet).
PhysXGasEmitter3D..density: Density injected each step (clamped up to at least this, never down -- the emitter tops a cell up, it does not overwrite a denser one).
PhysXGasEmitter3D..divergence: Outward-radial speed (m/s) from this node's position, added on top of velocity -- an explosion/burst emitter wants every cell pushed away from center, not all pushed the same direction.
PhysXGasEmitter3D..swirl: Tangential speed (m/s) around world +Y through this node's position -- directly authors rotation instead of relying on vorticity confinement to amplify whatever incidental curl the injection jitter happens to seed.
PhysXGasEmitter3D: A placement marker for one PhysXGas3D injection point, provided by the PhysX module.

PhysXGranular3D..friction: Internal friction angle in degrees -- the steepest slope a pile holds.
PhysXGranular3D..hardness: Young's modulus of the grains, in pascals.
PhysXGranular3D..grain_cohesion: 0 is dry sand. Small values pack the grains like wet sand or snow, letting a pile hold a steeper face and a light object rest on top instead of sinking.
PhysXGranular3D..density: Bulk density of the medium in kg/m³ -- the "weight" of the grains.
PhysXGranular3D: A GPU granular volume simulated by the PhysX physics backend -- sand, gravel or snow.

PhysXMotorcycle3D.is_sleeping: Returns whether the underlying PhysX vehicle actor is currently sleeping.
PhysXMotorcycle3D.get_linear_velocity: Current world-space linear velocity of the chassis.
PhysXMotorcycle3D.get_forward_speed: Current speed along the bike's own forward axis, in m/s.
PhysXMotorcycle3D.get_wheel_jounce: How compressed wheel wheel's suspension is right now, from 0 (fully extended / max droop) to that wheel's own PhysXVehicleWheel3D.suspension_travel (fully compressed / bottomed out).
PhysXMotorcycle3D.get_wheel_separation: 0 when wheel wheel can reach the ground within its suspension travel.
PhysXMotorcycle3D.get_wheel_lateral_force: The raw PxVehicle2 tire lateral force PhysX itself computed for wheel wheel this tick, projected onto the chassis's own current right vector.
PhysXMotorcycle3D.get_wheel_lateral_speed: The sideways (lateral) slip speed of wheel wheel's contact patch, as PxVehicle2's own tire model computes it.
PhysXMotorcycle3D.get_wheel_lateral_direction: The world-space direction PxVehicle2's own tire model currently treats as "lateral" (sideways) for wheel wheel -- a ground-truth diagnostic for checking a balance controller's own assumptions against the real tire model.
PhysXMotorcycle3D.get_wheel_lateral_force_vector: Same as get_wheel_lateral_force, but as a full world-space vector instead of a scalar projected onto the chassis's right axis.
PhysXMotorcycle3D.get_wheel_lateral_velocity: Same as get_wheel_lateral_speed, but as a full world-space velocity vector.
PhysXMotorcycle3D.get_wheel_camber_angle: Current camber angle of wheel wheel, in radians.
PhysXMotorcycle3D.get_actor_position: The real PhysX actor's own world-space origin -- for comparing against this node's own Node3D.global_position (which tracks the same point) when diagnosing a suspension/placement issue.
PhysXMotorcycle3D.apply_torque_impulse: Applies an instantaneous world-space angular impulse -- one of the tools a script-side lean/balance controller can use to correct roll.
PhysXMotorcycle3D.apply_force_at_local_position: Applies a continuous world-space force at local_position (in the body's own local/rotated frame, e.g.
PhysXMotorcycle3D.set_angular_velocity: Directly sets the chassis's world-space angular velocity -- the main tool a script-side lean/balance controller uses to correct roll every tick.
PhysXMotorcycle3D.get_angular_velocity: Current world-space angular velocity of the chassis -- read this every tick in a balance controller to measure the current roll/pitch/yaw rate.
PhysXMotorcycle3D.get_up: Current world-space up direction of the chassis.
PhysXMotorcycle3D.get_forward: Current world-space forward direction of the chassis.
PhysXMotorcycle3D.get_roll_angle: The chassis's current lean/roll angle, in radians, isolating rotation about the forward axis regardless of yaw (exact when pitch is small, the practical case a lean controller cares about).
PhysXMotorcycle3D..mass: Total mass of the motorcycle, in kg.
PhysXMotorcycle3D..moment_of_inertia: The vehicle's own rotational inertia around its X/Y/Z axes.
PhysXMotorcycle3D..center_of_mass_mode: Whether to derive the center of mass from the chassis CollisionShape3D position (Auto) or use center_of_mass directly (Custom).
PhysXMotorcycle3D..center_of_mass: The vehicle center of mass in the vehicle's local coordinates when center_of_mass_mode is Custom.
PhysXMotorcycle3D..can_sleep: Whether the vehicle is allowed to sleep after remaining below the PhysX space's configured sleep thresholds.
PhysXMotorcycle3D..max_engine_torque: The drive torque applied to the rear (traction) wheel when throttle is 1 -- the drivetrain is fixed rear-only regardless of PhysXVehicleWheel3D.use_as_traction's value on either wheel; that flag is read only for the fron
PhysXMotorcycle3D..max_brake_torque: The braking torque applied to each wheel when brake is 1.
PhysXMotorcycle3D..max_steer_angle: The steering angle, in radians, applied to the front wheel when steer is 1 or -1.
PhysXMotorcycle3D..reverse: Switches the drivetrain's gear between forward and reverse -- a real gear change (PxVehicle2 has no neutral-coast/instant-reverse shortcut), so throttle in reverse gear still needs to first bring the bike to a stop if it
PhysXMotorcycle3D: A PhysX-specific 2-wheel vehicle (motorcycle-style), powered by PxVehicle2 -- the same real per-wheel suspension/tire/drivetrain composition PhysXVehicle3D offers for 4 wheels, ported to a 2-wheel layout PhysXVehicle3D i

PhysXParticleFluid3D.spawn: Fills spawn_region_size, centered on the node, with a jittered grid of particles spaced particle_size apart (up to particle_count).
PhysXParticleFluid3D.get_live_particle_count: Returns the number of particles currently simulated.
PhysXParticleFluid3D.get_mpm_step_msec: Returns how long the last MPM solve took on the GPU, in milliseconds (submit plus wait).
PhysXParticleFluid3D.get_particle_positions: Returns the world-space position of every live particle, as read back from the GPU after the last physics step.
PhysXParticleFluid3D.get_submersion: Returns the fraction (0 to 1) of the given world-space box currently filled with fluid, estimated from the number of particles inside it.
PhysXParticleFluid3D.get_live_foam_count: Returns the number of diffuse (foam, spray, bubble) particles currently alive.
PhysXParticleFluid3D..solver: Which fluid solver simulates the particles.
PhysXParticleFluid3D..particle_size: Rest distance between neighboring particles, in meters.
PhysXParticleFluid3D..mpm_domain_size: MPM solver only. The MPM fluid is boundless — its grid follows the fluid, so this no longer confines it.
PhysXParticleFluid3D..mpm_substeps: MPM solver only. Simulation substeps per physics frame.
PhysXParticleFluid3D..mpm_stiffness: MPM solver only. Pressure stiffness of the weakly-compressible fluid.
PhysXParticleFluid3D..mpm_colliders: MPM solver only. PhysicsBody3D (or CollisionShape3D) nodes the fluid collides with, resolved to an analytic sphere, box, capsule or plane from each node's first shape.
PhysXParticleFluid3D..mpm_auto_colliders: MPM solver only. When enabled, the fluid also collides with every non-static PhysicsBody3D overlapping mpm_domain_size each step — the player, thrown objects, moving platforms — without listing them in mpm_colliders, the
PhysXParticleFluid3D..spawn_region_size: Size of the box, centered on the node, that spawn fills with particles.
PhysXParticleFluid3D..spawn_on_ready: When enabled, spawn runs automatically the first time the node enters the world outside the editor.
PhysXParticleFluid3D..emitting: When enabled, the node continuously streams new particles from its origin, acting as a faucet or hose.
PhysXParticleFluid3D..emission_rate: Number of particles spawned per second while emitting.
PhysXParticleFluid3D..emission_radius: Radius of the disc around the node origin that streamed particles spawn within, in meters.
PhysXParticleFluid3D..emission_velocity: Initial velocity given to streamed particles, in node-local space (it is rotated by the node's global transform).
PhysXParticleFluid3D..surface_mesh: When enabled, PhysX marching-cubes a smooth triangle mesh from the particles on the GPU (position smoothing + PxIsosurfaceExtractor, plus optional surface_anisotropy) and this node draws that instead of the sphere MultiM
PhysXParticleFluid3D..surface_anisotropy: Only used when surface_mesh is enabled.
PhysXParticleFluid3D..foam_enabled: When enabled, the solver spawns diffuse particles — foam, spray and bubbles — wherever the fluid is agitated enough (splashes, streams hitting a pool, fast-moving crests).
PhysXParticleFluid3D..foam_lifetime: How long, in seconds, a diffuse particle lives before it disappears.
PhysXParticleFluid3D..foam_threshold: How agitated the fluid must be locally before diffuse particles spawn there.
PhysXParticleFluid3D..foam_buoyancy: How strongly bubble-type foam particles (those below the surface) rise back up, from 0 to 1.
PhysXParticleFluid3D..foam_size: Froth clump scale, in meters, for the foam layer — independent of particle_size.
PhysXParticleFluid3D..viscosity: Resistance to flow. Higher values make the fluid thicker and slower, like honey.
PhysXParticleFluid3D..surface_tension: Strength of the force that minimizes the fluid's surface area, rounding off droplets and edges.
PhysXParticleFluid3D: A GPU position-based fluid simulated by the PhysX physics backend.

PhysXSkinnedCloth3D.get_effective_max_distances: The max distances the cloth will be built with, one per vertex of surface: max_distances if it has one value per vertex, otherwise the vertex colors if use_vertex_color is on and the mesh has them, otherwise compute_heig
PhysXSkinnedCloth3D.compute_height_ramp: The automatic max distances, one per vertex of surface: 0 at and above pin_height, rising linearly to max_distance at the mesh's lowest point.
PhysXSkinnedCloth3D.rebuild: Rebuilds the cloth from the source mesh on the next frame (after changing the mesh or its painted distances).
PhysXSkinnedCloth3D.reset: Puts the cloth back on the animated pose at rest, e.g.
PhysXSkinnedCloth3D.get_particle_count: The number of simulated particles: the surface's vertices with seams (split UV/normal vertices at the same position) welded together.
PhysXSkinnedCloth3D.get_body_capsules: The colliders the cloth uses, for debugging: one Dictionary per capsule with bone_a, bone_b, radius_a, radius_b and from_physical_bone.
PhysXSkinnedCloth3D..mesh_instance_path: The skinned MeshInstance3D whose surface is simulated.
PhysXSkinnedCloth3D..surface: Which surface of the mesh is the cloth.
PhysXSkinnedCloth3D..max_distances: Painted max distance (meters) per vertex of surface, in the mesh's vertex order: how far each vertex may stray from its animated position.
PhysXSkinnedCloth3D..pin_height: Automatic painting: vertices at or above this height in the mesh's bind pose (meters) follow the animation exactly.
PhysXSkinnedCloth3D..max_distance: The largest max distance (meters) of the automatic painting: the ramp's value at the mesh's lowest point (it rises linearly from 0 at pin_height), and the value a vertex colour of 1 maps to with use_vertex_color.
PhysXSkinnedCloth3D..use_vertex_color: When max_distances isn't painted, take each vertex's max distance from the red channel of the mesh's vertex colour times max_distance, so distances painted in a modeling tool carry over.
PhysXSkinnedCloth3D..damping: Fraction of the cloth's motion relative to the animated garment lost per second: settles swinging and jiggle.
PhysXSkinnedCloth3D..thickness: Extra distance (meters) the cloth keeps from the body capsules.
PhysXSkinnedCloth3D..simulating: Pauses the simulation when off (the cloth holds its last shape).
PhysXSkinnedCloth3D..collide_with_body: Collide the cloth with the character's physical bones (or the automatic capsules).
PhysXSkinnedCloth3D..body_mesh_path: Optional skinned MeshInstance3D of the character's body.
PhysXSkinnedCloth3D..collision_radius_scale: Scales the automatic capsules' radii (not the physical bones' shapes, which are used as they are).
PhysXSkinnedCloth3D..backstop: How far (meters) the cloth may sink inward past its animated position, measured along the animated surface's normal.
PhysXSkinnedCloth3D..animation_drive: How strongly free cloth is pulled back toward its animated shape: the fraction of the way back per 1/60 s, 0..1.
PhysXSkinnedCloth3D..self_collision: Keep the cloth from passing through itself where it folds and gathers: particles closer than self_collision_thickness are pushed apart, unless they're that close in the garment itself.
PhysXSkinnedCloth3D..self_collision_thickness: How far apart (meters) the cloth keeps its own layers with self_collision on.
PhysXSkinnedCloth3D: Cloth on a region of a character's skinned mesh -- a robe, cape or skirt that moves with the animation and swings and drapes on its own.

PhysXTank3D.is_sleeping: Returns whether the underlying PhysX vehicle actor is currently sleeping.
PhysXTank3D.get_linear_velocity: Current world-space linear velocity of the hull.
PhysXTank3D.get_angular_velocity: Current world-space angular velocity of the hull.
PhysXTank3D.get_forward_speed: Current speed along the hull's own forward axis, in m/s.
PhysXTank3D.get_up: Current world-space up direction of the hull.
PhysXTank3D.get_forward: Current world-space forward direction of the hull.
PhysXTank3D.get_wheel_jounce: How compressed wheel wheel's suspension is right now, from 0 (fully extended / max droop) to that wheel's own PhysXVehicleWheel3D.suspension_travel (fully compressed / bottomed out).
PhysXTank3D.get_wheel_separation: 0 when wheel wheel can reach the ground within its suspension travel.
PhysXTank3D.get_actor_position: The real PhysX actor's own world-space origin -- for comparing against this node's own Node3D.global_position (which tracks the same point) when diagnosing a suspension/placement issue.
PhysXTank3D..mass: Total mass of the tank, in kg.
PhysXTank3D..moment_of_inertia: The vehicle's own rotational inertia around its X/Y/Z axes.
PhysXTank3D..center_of_mass_mode: Whether to derive the center of mass from the hull CollisionShape3D position (Auto) or use center_of_mass directly (Custom).
PhysXTank3D..center_of_mass: The vehicle center of mass in the vehicle's local coordinates when center_of_mass_mode is Custom.
PhysXTank3D..can_sleep: Whether the vehicle is allowed to sleep after remaining below the PhysX space's configured sleep thresholds.
PhysXTank3D..max_engine_torque: The total drive torque a fully-throttled track produces, split evenly across that track's own wheels -- see left_ratio/right_ratio.
PhysXTank3D..max_brake_torque: The braking torque applied to each wheel when brake is 1.
PhysXTank3D..left_ratio: Drive input for the left track, -1 to 1.
PhysXTank3D..right_ratio: Drive input for the right track, -1 to 1.
PhysXTank3D: A PhysX-specific tracked (tank-style) vehicle, powered by PxVehicle2 -- the same real per-wheel suspension/tire/drivetrain composition PhysXVehicle3D and PhysXMotorcycle3D offer, driven entirely by skid-steer instead of

PhysXVehicle3D.is_sleeping: Returns whether the underlying PhysX vehicle actor is currently sleeping.
PhysXVehicle3D.get_linear_velocity: Current world-space linear velocity of the chassis.
PhysXVehicle3D.get_forward_speed: Current speed along the car's own forward axis, in m/s.
PhysXVehicle3D.get_wheel_jounce: How compressed wheel wheel's suspension is right now, from 0 (fully extended / max droop) to that wheel's own PhysXVehicleWheel3D.suspension_travel (fully compressed / bottomed out).
PhysXVehicle3D.get_wheel_separation: 0 when wheel wheel can reach the ground within its suspension travel.
PhysXVehicle3D.get_actor_position: The real PhysX actor's own world-space origin -- for comparing against this node's own Node3D.global_position (which tracks the same point) when diagnosing a suspension/placement issue.
PhysXVehicle3D..mass: Total mass of the vehicle, in kg.
PhysXVehicle3D..moment_of_inertia: The vehicle's own rotational inertia around its X/Y/Z axes.
PhysXVehicle3D..center_of_mass_mode: Whether to derive the center of mass from the chassis CollisionShape3D position (Auto) or use center_of_mass directly (Custom).
PhysXVehicle3D..center_of_mass: The vehicle center of mass in the vehicle's local coordinates when center_of_mass_mode is Custom.
PhysXVehicle3D..can_sleep: Whether the vehicle is allowed to sleep after remaining below the PhysX space's configured sleep thresholds.
PhysXVehicle3D..max_engine_torque: The drive torque applied to every wheel with PhysXVehicleWheel3D.use_as_traction enabled when throttle is 1 (a real direct-drive response, unlike VehicleBody3D.engine_force which is a raw force value with no torque curve
PhysXVehicle3D..max_brake_torque: The braking torque applied to each wheel when brake is 1.
PhysXVehicle3D..max_steer_angle: The steering angle, in radians, applied to the front axle when steer is 1 or -1.
PhysXVehicle3D..ackermann_strength: How much Ackermann steering correction to apply to the front (steering) axle, from 0 (both front wheels always turn by the same angle, like VehicleWheel3D) to 1 (full correction: the inside wheel of a turn steers more sh
PhysXVehicle3D..front_anti_roll_stiffness: Anti-roll bar stiffness connecting the front-left and front-right wheels.
PhysXVehicle3D..rear_anti_roll_stiffness: Same as front_anti_roll_stiffness, connecting the rear-left and rear-right wheels instead.
PhysXVehicle3D..reverse: Switches the drivetrain's gear between forward and reverse -- a real gear change (PxVehicle2 has no neutral-coast/instant-reverse shortcut), so throttle in reverse gear still needs to first bring the car to a stop if it
PhysXVehicle3D: A PhysX-specific 4-wheel vehicle, powered by PxVehicle2 -- an alternative to the stock, backend-agnostic VehicleBody3D, not a replacement for it.

PhysXVehicleWheel3D..radius: The wheel's radius, in meters -- also the size the suspension raycast uses to place the wheel above the ground, so this should match whatever wheel mesh is parented under this node.
PhysXVehicleWheel3D..half_width: Half the wheel's thickness, in meters.
PhysXVehicleWheel3D..wheel_mass: The wheel's own mass, in kg -- affects how quickly it spins up/down under engine torque or braking, independent of the vehicle's own PhysXVehicle3D.mass.
PhysXVehicleWheel3D..wheel_moment_of_inertia: The wheel's own rotational inertia around its axle -- higher values make its spin speed change more sluggishly under engine torque or braking.
PhysXVehicleWheel3D..damping_rate: Damping applied to the wheel's own spin (rotation around its axle), independent of the tire's road grip -- resists the wheel spinning up or down, similar to driveline/bearing friction.
PhysXVehicleWheel3D..suspension_travel: How far the suspension can move from full droop to full compression, in meters -- matches PhysX's own reference vehicle.
PhysXVehicleWheel3D..suspension_stiffness: The suspension spring's stiffness, in N/m.
PhysXVehicleWheel3D..suspension_damping: How strongly the suspension resists the *rate* of compression change, separate from suspension_stiffness's resistance to compression itself -- higher values settle bounces (from a bump, or landing after a jump) faster, w
PhysXVehicleWheel3D..tire_lateral_stiffness: How much sideways (cornering) force the tire develops per unit of lateral slip angle.
PhysXVehicleWheel3D..tire_longitudinal_stiffness: How much forward/backward (acceleration or braking) force the tire develops per unit of longitudinal slip.
PhysXVehicleWheel3D..tire_camber_stiffness: How much lateral force the tire develops from camber angle.
PhysXVehicleWheel3D..tire_friction: The tire's peak grip coefficient, reached at ~10% wheel slip.
PhysXVehicleWheel3D..tire_rest_grip: Grip at zero wheel slip, as a fraction of tire_friction.
PhysXVehicleWheel3D..tire_slide_grip: Grip once the tire is fully sliding/locked (100% wheel slip), as a fraction of tire_friction.
PhysXVehicleWheel3D..use_as_steering: Whether this wheel is on the steering (front) axle.
PhysXVehicleWheel3D..use_as_traction: Whether this wheel receives engine torque from PhysXVehicle3D.throttle.

PhysXWaterSpray3D..water_surface_path: The PhysXWaterSurface3D the spray comes off.
PhysXWaterSpray3D..bow_emitters: GPUParticles3D nodes that spray with forward speed while their part of the hull is in the water.
PhysXWaterSpray3D..stern_emitters: GPUParticles3D nodes that spray with a sibling PhysXBoat3D's propeller thrust.
PhysXWaterSpray3D..slam_emitters: One-shot GPUParticles3D nodes restarted when the hull drops back onto the water.
PhysXWaterSpray3D..start_speed: The forward speed (m/s) below which there is no bow spray.
PhysXWaterSpray3D..reference_speed: The forward speed (m/s) at which bow spray reaches its full rate and launch speed.
PhysXWaterSpray3D..slow_velocity_scale: The share of an emitter's launch speed used at low speed (or low thrust, for stern emitters), rising to all of it at reference_speed.
PhysXWaterSpray3D..submerge_depth: How far (m) above the water an emitter's place on the hull can rise before it stops spraying, easing out over that height.
PhysXWaterSpray3D..slam_speed: How fast (m/s) the hull has to close on the water as it drops back in for a slam to fire.
PhysXWaterSpray3D..slam_full_speed: The closing speed (m/s) at which a slam fires at full strength.
PhysXWaterSpray3D..slam_cooldown: Seconds before a slam emitter can fire again.
PhysXWaterSpray3D..water_collision: If true, a GPUParticlesCollisionBox3D follows the hull with its top on the water, for emitters whose process material collides to land on.
PhysXWaterSpray3D..collision_size: The side length (m) of the water collider around the hull.
PhysXWaterSpray3D..collision_fit_radius: How far (m) either side of the hull the water is sampled to fit the collision plane to the waves.
PhysXWaterSpray3D..collision_margin: How far (m) above the collision plane emitters are held with water_collision on.
PhysXWaterSpray3D..collision_smoothing: Seconds over which the collision plane eases to the water's fitted height and slope.
PhysXWaterSpray3D..spray_foam: How white (0 to 1) each speck of foam the landing spray leaves starts.
PhysXWaterSpray3D..spray_foam_density: The chance, per launch spot per physics tick at full spray, of a speck of foam: lower for sparser, stirred-looking water.
PhysXWaterSpray3D..spray_foam_offset: How much further out (m) than the spray lands the foam is placed.
PhysXWaterSpray3D.!slammed: Emitted when the hull drops back onto the water hard enough to fire the slam emitters: where, on the water, and how fast (m/s) it closed on it -- for a splash sound, a camera shake.
PhysXWaterSpray3D: Drives GPUParticles3D spray from a hull moving through a PhysXWaterSurface3D.

PhysXWaterSurface3D.get_effective_fetch: The fetch (meters of open water the wind blows over) the wave spectrum actually uses: fetch when it's above 0, otherwise the automatic value -- the longest side of the surface_mesh footprint for enclosed water, or 100 km
PhysXWaterSurface3D.get_caustics_light_right: Light-space horizontal projection axis used to sample get_caustics_texture.
PhysXWaterSurface3D.get_caustics_light_up: Light-space vertical projection axis used to sample get_caustics_texture.
PhysXWaterSurface3D.get_caustics_origin: World-space center of the light-space caustics projection.
PhysXWaterSurface3D.get_caustics_half_extent: Half-width of the square light-space projection in world units, used to map receiver positions to get_caustics_texture UV coordinates.
PhysXWaterSurface3D.get_caustics_tile_size: The caustics repeat with the ocean waves, every ocean_domain_size.
PhysXWaterSurface3D.sample_height: The combined surface height (ripple + ocean layers, plus water_level) at world_pos's XZ, bilinearly sampled from the last readback (refreshed every physics tick, a few frames behind the GPU simulation -- fine for buoyanc
PhysXWaterSurface3D.is_wet: Whether there is water at world_pos's XZ, at the ripple grid's resolution: inside the surface_mesh footprint, and not over dry seabed (seabed_from_floor).
PhysXWaterSurface3D.submit_sphere: A persistent body proxy that pushes the ripple layer's surface down near world_pos's XZ, proportional to radius and strength.
PhysXWaterSurface3D.clear_sphere: Removes a previously-submitted sphere proxy (see submit_sphere) by its owner id.
PhysXWaterSurface3D.submit_impulse: A one-shot local disturbance (a splash) at world_pos's XZ -- consumed by the next simulation step, then cleared automatically.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..surface_mesh: Optional water outline: any flat Mesh (node-local) whose up-facing triangles' X/Z footprint is the water -- e.g.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..domain_size: World-space extent (X, Z) of the local ripple layer -- independent of ocean_domain_size, see ocean_grid_resolution's own note on why.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..grid_resolution: Cell count per side of the local ripple layer's grid.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..depth: Still-water depth in meters used everywhere unless seabed_from_floor measures it per cell (then it only applies where no floor is found below the water).
PhysXWaterSurface3D..water_level: Mean world-space Y of the surface -- place the node here rather than relying on its own transform, since the rendered mesh and both simulation layers are displaced relative to this baseline.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..damping: Damping (ALPHA) on the local ripple layer's wave equation -- higher settles disturbances faster.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..ripple_amplitude: Multiplier on the ripple displacement driven by submitted floating-body proxies and impulses.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..seabed_from_floor: When on, the still-water depth of each ripple cell is measured on the first physics tick by a ray straight down onto the static bodies in seabed_collision_mask, starting 100 m above the water.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..shallow_fade_depth: Water shallower than this many meters fades the ocean chop out, down to none at the waterline, so the surface meets a beach calmly instead of the chop cutting through the sand.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..ocean_grid_resolution: Cell count per side of the FFT ocean layer's grid.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..ocean_domain_size: World-space extent (X, Z) of the FFT ocean layer -- also the size of the rendered PlaneMesh.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..wind_speed: Wind speed in m/s driving the FFT ocean layer's spectrum -- higher produces longer, larger waves, up to what fetch allows.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..wind_direction: Direction (X, Z) the wind blows toward; the FFT ocean waves are aligned with it and travel downwind.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..wave_amplitude: Linear height multiplier for the FFT ocean waves.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..fetch: How far the wind has blown over open water, in meters.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..choppiness: Tessendorf horizontal displacement of the ocean layer: pulls the surface toward the wave crests so they sharpen and the troughs flatten, the way real wind waves look.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..foam_enabled: Whether whitecap foam forms at all.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..foam_threshold: How squeezed the surface must be before whitecap foam forms: foam is injected where the choppy displacement's area Jacobian drops below this (1 = unsqueezed, 0 = folding over).
PhysXWaterSurface3D..shore_foam_band: Shore foam: where the still water is shallower than this many meters, each arriving wave crest leaves a thin, lacy foam sheet at the waterline that moves with the water (see shore_undertow), carries on up the swash onto
PhysXWaterSurface3D..shore_undertow: Steady seaward drift (m/s) of the shore foam.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..foam_persistence: Time constant in seconds over which whitecap foam fades once its wave has passed.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..swash_run_up: Swash: the bigger arriving waves (the crests well above the usual ones, so it comes in sets) run up past the still-water line onto the dry sand as a thin film, at most this high (m above still water, not distance along t
PhysXWaterSurface3D..swash_drain_speed: How fast (m/s, vertical) the swash slides back down the sand after a wave has run up.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..wet_sand_dry_time: Time constant (s) for sand uncovered by the swash to dry: the wet darkening fades to about a third over this long.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..render_extent: Side length in meters of the rendered surface, centered on the simulation, for open water that runs to the horizon.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..normal_mode: How the surface's normals and whitecap foam are computed, set on the material through its per_pixel_normals uniform.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..water_material: The material driving the surface mesh's displacement/shading.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..caustics_enabled: Enables the light-space caustics draw pass and its render target.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..caustics_sun_direction: World-space direction that light travels from the source toward the water.
PhysXWaterSurface3D..caustics_reference_depth: Approximate distance the refracted light travels below the surface before it is mapped into the caustics texture.
PhysXWaterSurface3D: A real animated water surface: a GPU FFT ocean spectrum layer plus a local ripple layer that bodies can disturb, rendered as a displaced mesh.

PhysXWaterWake3D.add_foam: Churns foam into the wake's water around world_position on the next physics step: amount_per_second at the center (1 is fully white), fading out over radius meters.
PhysXWaterWake3D.sample_height: The wake's height (m) at world_pos's XZ, from the last readback (a few frames behind the simulation); 0 outside the grid.
PhysXWaterWake3D.get_grid_origin: The world XZ of the grid's corner, as last stepped.
PhysXWaterWake3D.get_height_texture: The wake's texture, as the water material draws it: red the height (m), green the hull foam, blue the propeller foam (0 to 1).
PhysXWaterWake3D..cells: Grid cells per side. With size this sets the cell size: keep it around 0.25 m for crisp foam and short wake waves.
PhysXWaterWake3D..wave_speed: How fast (m/s) the wake's waves travel.
PhysXWaterWake3D..damping: How quickly the wake's waves die out, per second.
PhysXWaterWake3D..border_damping: Damping per second at the grid's edge, easing in across the outer tenth of it: waves running into the border are absorbed instead of reflecting back at the body.
PhysXWaterWake3D..shore_grid_fade: How much the wake fades out over the water surface's simulated shore square: 0 draws it everywhere (open water, an ocean), 1 leaves that square to the body's PhysXBuoyancy3D ripples (a lake, where the interactive ripples
PhysXWaterWake3D..bow_foam: Hull foam churned in per second at the bow, along the hull's sides, at reference_speed; it tapers off toward the stern and scales with speed.
PhysXWaterWake3D..propeller_foam: Propeller foam churned in per second at full thrust, behind a sibling PhysXBoat3D's propeller.
PhysXWaterWake3D..foam_persistence: Seconds the foam takes to fade to about a third.
PhysXWaterWake3D..foam_slope: The wake wave slope past which waves break into hull foam.
PhysXWaterWake3D..foam_slope_gain: Foam per second per unit of slope past foam_slope.
PhysXWaterWake3D..foam_spread: How fast (m/s) the hull foam is pushed out sideways from the hull's line at full speed -- strongest near the hull, fading out over about three beams -- so it opens into two bands behind the boat.
PhysXWaterWake3D..source_count: How many dips the hull is pushed down as, spread along its keel from bow to stern.
PhysXWaterWake3D..rest_depth: How far (m) the hull pushes the water down at rest.
PhysXWaterWake3D..wake_depth: How far (m) the hull pushes the water down at the bow at reference_speed; shallower toward the stern.
PhysXWaterWake3D..reference_speed: The speed (m/s) at which the hull dips to wake_depth and churns bow_foam; faster goes up to 1.5 times that.
PhysXWaterWake3D: The wake and foam a RigidBody3D leaves on a PhysXWaterSurface3D as it moves.

RenderingServer.mesh_surface_get_format_index_stride: Returns the stride of the index buffer for a mesh with the given format.

RenderingServer.mesh_add_surface_from_arrays: Creates a new surface on the given mesh.

RenderingServer.mesh_set_blend_shape_mode: Sets a mesh's blend shape mode.
RenderingServer.mesh_get_blend_shape_mode: Returns a mesh's blend shape mode.

RenderingServer.mesh_surface_get_arrays: Returns a mesh's surface's buffer arrays.
RenderingServer.mesh_surface_get_blend_shape_arrays: Returns a mesh's surface's arrays for blend shapes.
RenderingServer.mesh_get_surface_count: Returns a mesh's number of surfaces.

RenderingServer.mesh_clear: Removes all surfaces from a mesh.

RenderingServer.mesh_surface_update_attribute_region: Updates the attribute buffer of the mesh surface with the given data.
RenderingServer.mesh_surface_update_skin_region: Updates the skin buffer of the mesh surface with the given data.
RenderingServer.mesh_surface_update_index_region: Updates the index buffer of the mesh surface with the given data.

RenderingServer.mesh_surface_get_attribute_buffer_rd_rid: Returns the RenderingDevice RID handle of the attribute buffer of the given mesh surface (Color, UV, UV2, Custom0-3).
RenderingServer.mesh_surface_get_skin_buffer_rd_rid: Returns the RenderingDevice RID handle of the skin buffer of the given mesh surface (Bones, Weights).
RenderingServer.mesh_surface_get_index_buffer_rd_rid: Returns the RenderingDevice RID handle of the index buffer of the given mesh surface.
RenderingServer.mesh_set_shadow_mesh: Sets an optional second mesh which can be used for rendering shadows and the depth prepass.
RenderingServer.multimesh_create: Creates a new multimesh on the RenderingServer and returns an RID handle.
RenderingServer.multimesh_allocate_data: Sets up the multimesh using the specified data.
RenderingServer.multimesh_get_instance_count: Returns the number of instances allocated for this multimesh.
RenderingServer.multimesh_set_mesh: Sets the mesh to be drawn by the multimesh.
RenderingServer.multimesh_instance_set_transform: Sets the Transform3D for this instance.
RenderingServer.multimesh_instance_set_transform_2d: Sets the Transform2D for this instance.

RenderingServer.multimesh_instance_set_custom_data: Sets the custom data for this instance.
RenderingServer.multimesh_get_mesh: Returns the RID of the mesh that will be used in drawing this multimesh.
RenderingServer.multimesh_get_aabb: Calculates and returns the axis-aligned bounding box that encloses all instances within the multimesh.
RenderingServer.multimesh_set_custom_aabb: Sets the custom AABB for this MultiMesh resource.
RenderingServer.multimesh_get_custom_aabb: Returns the custom AABB defined for this MultiMesh resource.
RenderingServer.multimesh_instance_get_transform: Returns the Transform3D of the specified instance.
RenderingServer.multimesh_instance_get_transform_2d: Returns the Transform2D of the specified instance.
RenderingServer.multimesh_instance_get_color: Returns the color by which the specified instance will be modulated.
RenderingServer.multimesh_instance_get_custom_data: Returns the custom data associated with the specified instance.
RenderingServer.multimesh_set_visible_instances: Sets the number of instances visible at a given time.
RenderingServer.multimesh_get_visible_instances: Returns the number of visible instances for this multimesh.
RenderingServer.multimesh_set_buffer: Set the entire data to use for drawing the multimesh at once to buffer (such as instance transforms and colors).
RenderingServer.multimesh_get_command_buffer_rd_rid: Returns the RenderingDevice RID handle of the MultiMesh command buffer.
RenderingServer.multimesh_get_buffer_rd_rid: Returns the RenderingDevice RID handle of the MultiMesh, which can be used as any other buffer on the Rendering Device.
RenderingServer.multimesh_get_buffer: Returns the MultiMesh data (such as instance transforms, colors, etc.).

RenderingServer.multimesh_set_physics_interpolated: Turns on and off physics interpolation for this MultiMesh resource.
RenderingServer.multimesh_set_physics_interpolation_qual: Sets the physics interpolation quality for the MultiMesh.
RenderingServer.multimesh_instance_reset_physics_interpo: Prevents physics interpolation for the specified instance during the current physics tick.
RenderingServer.multimesh_instances_reset_physics_interp: Prevents physics interpolation for all instances during the current physics tick.
RenderingServer.skeleton_create: Creates a skeleton and adds it to the RenderingServer.

RenderingServer.skeleton_set_base_transform_2d: Sets the base Transform2D to use for the specified skeleton.
RenderingServer.directional_light_create: Creates a directional light and adds it to the RenderingServer.

RenderingServer.spot_light_create: Creates a spot light and adds it to the RenderingServer.
RenderingServer.area_light_create: Creates a new area light and adds it to the RenderingServer.

RenderingServer.light_set_shadow: If true, light will cast shadows.

RenderingServer.light_set_negative: If true, the 3D light will subtract light instead of adding light.
RenderingServer.light_set_cull_mask: Sets the cull mask for this 3D light.
RenderingServer.light_set_distance_fade: Sets the distance fade for this 3D light.

RenderingServer.light_set_bake_mode: Sets the bake mode to use for the specified 3D light.

RenderingServer.light_set_allow_contact_shadows: If true, allows screen-space contact shadows for this light.
RenderingServer.light_omni_set_shadow_mode: Sets whether to use a dual paraboloid or a cubemap for the shadow map.
RenderingServer.light_directional_set_shadow_mode: Sets the shadow mode for this directional light.
RenderingServer.light_directional_set_blend_splits: If true, this directional light will blend between shadow map splits resulting in a smoother transition between them.
RenderingServer.light_directional_set_sky_mode: If true, this light will not be used for anything except sky shaders.
RenderingServer.light_area_set_size: Sets the extents (width and height) in meters for this area light.
RenderingServer.light_area_set_normalize_energy: Defines whether the energy of an AreaLight3D is normalized (divided) by its area.
RenderingServer.light_projectors_set_filter: Sets the texture filter mode to use when rendering light projectors.
RenderingServer.lightmaps_set_bicubic_filter: Toggles whether a bicubic filter should be used when lightmaps are sampled.
RenderingServer.positional_soft_shadow_filter_set_qualit: Sets the filter quality for omni and spot light shadows in 3D.
RenderingServer.directional_soft_shadow_filter_set_quali: Sets the filter quality for directional light shadows in 3D.
RenderingServer.directional_shadow_atlas_set_size: Sets the size of the directional light shadows in 3D.
RenderingServer.reflection_probe_create: Creates a reflection probe and adds it to the RenderingServer.
RenderingServer.reflection_probe_set_update_mode: Sets how often the reflection probe updates.
RenderingServer.reflection_probe_set_intensity: Sets the intensity of the reflection probe.
RenderingServer.reflection_probe_set_blend_distance: Sets the distance in meters over which a probe blends into the scene.
RenderingServer.reflection_probe_set_ambient_mode: Sets the reflection probe's ambient light mode.

RenderingServer.reflection_probe_set_size: Sets the size of the area that the reflection probe will capture.
RenderingServer.reflection_probe_set_origin_offset: Sets the origin offset to be used when this reflection probe is in box project mode.
RenderingServer.reflection_probe_set_as_interior: If true, reflections will ignore sky contribution.
RenderingServer.reflection_probe_set_enable_shadows: If true, computes shadows in the reflection probe.
RenderingServer.reflection_probe_set_cull_mask: Sets the render cull mask for this reflection probe.
RenderingServer.reflection_probe_set_reflection_mask: Sets the render reflection mask for this reflection probe.
RenderingServer.reflection_probe_set_mesh_lod_threshold: Sets the mesh level of detail to use in the reflection probe rendering.

RenderingServer.decal_set_emission_energy: Sets the emission energy in the decal specified by the decal RID.

RenderingServer.decals_set_filter: Sets the texture filter mode to use when rendering decals.

RenderingServer.voxel_gi_create: Creates a new voxel-based global illumination object and adds it to the RenderingServer.

RenderingServer.voxel_gi_get_octree_size: Returns the octree size for the specified voxel GI data instance, which corresponds to the number of subdivisions per axis.
RenderingServer.voxel_gi_get_octree_cells: Returns the octree cell data for the specified voxel GI data instance.

RenderingServer.voxel_gi_get_distance_field: Returns the distance field data for the specified voxel GI data instance.

RenderingServer.voxel_gi_get_to_cell_xform: Returns the transform to cell space for the specified voxel GI data instance.
RenderingServer.voxel_gi_set_dynamic_range: Sets the VoxelGIData.dynamic_range value to use on the specified voxel_gi's RID.
RenderingServer.voxel_gi_set_propagation: Sets the VoxelGIData.propagation value to use on the specified voxel_gi's RID.

RenderingServer.voxel_gi_set_baked_exposure_normalizatio: Used to inform the renderer what exposure normalization value was used while baking the voxel gi.
RenderingServer.voxel_gi_set_bias: Sets the VoxelGIData.bias value to use on the specified voxel_gi's RID.
RenderingServer.voxel_gi_set_normal_bias: Sets the VoxelGIData.normal_bias value to use on the specified voxel_gi's RID.
RenderingServer.voxel_gi_set_interior: Sets the VoxelGIData.interior value to use on the specified voxel_gi's RID.
RenderingServer.voxel_gi_set_use_two_bounces: Sets the VoxelGIData.use_two_bounces value to use on the specified voxel_gi's RID.
RenderingServer.voxel_gi_set_quality: Sets the ProjectSettings.rendering/global_illumination/voxel_gi/quality value to use when rendering.

RenderingServer.lightmap_set_probe_interior: Sets whether the lightmap instance should be considered as interior (when interior is true).
RenderingServer.lightmap_set_probe_capture_data: Sets the probe capture data for the given lightmap instance.
RenderingServer.lightmap_get_probe_capture_points: Returns the local space positions of each lightmap probe capture point.

RenderingServer.lightmap_get_probe_capture_bsp_tree: Returns the BSP tree data used for accelerating probe lookups.
RenderingServer.lightmap_set_baked_exposure_normalizatio: Used to inform the renderer what exposure normalization value was used while baking the lightmap.
RenderingServer.lightmap_set_probe_capture_update_speed: The framerate-independent update speed when representing dynamic object lighting from LightmapProbes.
RenderingServer.particles_create: Creates a GPU-based particle system and adds it to the RenderingServer.
RenderingServer.particles_set_mode: Sets whether the GPU particles specified by the particles RID should be rendered in 2D or 3D according to mode.
RenderingServer.particles_set_emitting: If true, particles will emit over time.
RenderingServer.particles_get_emitting: Returns true if particles are currently set to emitting.
RenderingServer.particles_set_amount: Sets the number of particles to be drawn and allocates the memory for them.
RenderingServer.particles_set_amount_ratio: Sets the amount ratio for particles to be emitted.
RenderingServer.particles_set_lifetime: Sets the lifetime of each particle in the system.
RenderingServer.particles_set_one_shot: If true, particles will emit once and then stop.
RenderingServer.particles_set_pre_process_time: Sets the preprocess time for the particles' animation.
RenderingServer.particles_request_process_time: Requests the particles to process for extra process time during a single frame.
RenderingServer.particles_set_interp_to_end: Sets the value that informs a ParticleProcessMaterial to rush all particles towards the end of their lifetime.
RenderingServer.particles_set_emitter_velocity: Sets the velocity of a particle node, that will be used by ParticleProcessMaterial.inherit_velocity_ratio.
RenderingServer.particles_set_custom_aabb: Sets a custom axis-aligned bounding box for the particle system.
RenderingServer.particles_set_speed_scale: Sets the speed scale of the particle system.

RenderingServer.particles_set_process_material: Sets the material for processing the particles.
RenderingServer.particles_set_fixed_fps: Sets the frame rate that the particle system rendering will be fixed to.
RenderingServer.particles_set_interpolate: Sets whether particles should use interpolation between fixed steps.
RenderingServer.particles_set_fractional_delta: If true, uses fractional delta which smooths the movement of the particles.
RenderingServer.particles_set_collision_base_size: Sets the base size for particle collision.
RenderingServer.particles_set_transform_align: Sets the transform alignment for the particle system.
RenderingServer.particles_set_transform_align_channel_fi: When using Z-Billboarding, which CUSTOM channel to read from.
RenderingServer.particles_set_transform_align_axis: Sets which axis to use for transform alignment.
RenderingServer.particles_set_trails: If enable is true, enables trails for the particles with the specified length_sec in seconds.
RenderingServer.particles_set_trail_bind_poses: Sets the trail bind poses for the particle system.
RenderingServer.particles_is_inactive: Returns true if particles are not emitting and particles are set to inactive.
RenderingServer.particles_request_process: Add particle system to list of particle systems that need to be updated.
RenderingServer.particles_restart: Reset the particles on the next update.
RenderingServer.particles_set_subemitter: Sets the subemitter particles for the particle system.
RenderingServer.particles_emit: Manually emits particles from the particles instance.
RenderingServer.particles_set_draw_order: Sets the draw order of the particles.
RenderingServer.particles_set_draw_passes: Sets the number of draw passes to use.
RenderingServer.particles_set_draw_pass_mesh: Sets the mesh to be used for the specified draw pass.
RenderingServer.particles_get_current_aabb: Calculates and returns the axis-aligned bounding box that contains all the particles.
RenderingServer.particles_set_emission_transform: Sets the Transform3D that will be used by the particles when they first emit.
